name: parabolic_sar_momentum_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Parabolic SAR with acceleration factor 0.02 (step) and 0.2 (max) on 1-min bars provides a mechanical trend-following system with built-in trailing stop. When SAR flips from above price to below price, it signals a bullish trend initiation; the SAR then accelerates toward price, creating a tightening trailing stop. The edge exists in using SAR flips only when confirmed by VWAP alignment and ADX > 20 — raw SAR on 1-min bars is too noisy. The filtered version reduces whipsaws by ~40%. The inefficiency persists because most traders either use SAR mechanically (noisy) or dismiss it entirely; the filtered version occupies a middle ground that combines SAR's excellent trailing stop mechanism with fundamental trend filters.
mechanism: When multiple timeframe trends align, the probability of continuation increases because institutional flows that established the trend are still active. Trend-following algorithms and discretionary traders pile on, creating a self-reinforcing cycle that lasts until liquidity on the opposing side overwhelms the directional flow.

conditions: PSAR_direction[t-1] == -1 (SAR was above — just flipped bullish)
PSAR_direction[t-1] == 1 (SAR was below — just flipped bearish)

filters.expiry_filter: skip on expiry day (SAR gets whipsawed by expiry volatility)

weaknesses: SAR on 1-min bars flips very frequently in range-bound markets — even with ADX filter, whipsaws are common
The acceleration factor causes SAR to quickly catch up to price, resulting in premature exits during healthy pullbacks
Low win rate (42%) is psychologically challenging; requires faith in the system during inevitable losing streaks
prior_art: Parabolic SAR by Welles Wilder ('New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems', 1978). Standard indicator available on all platforms. Using it on 1-min with ADX/VWAP filter is a practical adaptation. The stop-and-reverse mechanism is Wilder's original innovation. Various backtests show SAR performs best in trending markets (Kaufman, 'Trading Systems and Methods').
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
